**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 10.3, ¶p0063), confidence 0.72.**

- **What's there:** Section 10.3 is only a successors-and-assigns binding provision. It imposes no restriction on assignment by either party and sets no consent standard.
- **What's fine:** Nothing prohibits our assignment or blocks an M&A transfer, and I confirmed (searches for "change of control," "terminate," and review of the term/termination provisions at ¶p0011, p0024, p0026) that HDI has no termination or re-pricing right triggered by our change of control — so this is not walk-away territory.
- **Why it still fails:** The fallback requires a consent-not-unreasonably-withheld standard. As drafted, HDI could transfer this site development and hosting engagement — including access to our confidential information and our customer-facing site — to any third party, including a competitor, without our consent.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** Appends to 10.3 an express carve-out permitting our assignment to an affiliate or M&A successor without consent, and conditions any HDI assignment on our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld), never to a competitor, with violating assignments void. The missing written-notice mechanic for successor assignments is noted in the rationale only, not flagged.
